exports.name: isEquipmentUnlocked
exports.doc: Checks whether a weapon, shield, quiver, or catalyst is unlocked/owned by the pilot. When `bypassProgressionGates` is enabled (or tutorial is toggled off in sandbox), all items are available.

exports.name: getOwnedWeaponCount
exports.doc: Returns how many separate instances of `weaponId` the pilot owns. Paired Stance (`main: sword1`, `side: sword1` in `1h` grip) requires 2 separate items.

exports.name: acquireAdditionalWeaponCopy
exports.doc: Grants or requisitions a second separate instance of a weapon so the pilot can enter Dual-Wield Paired Stance.

exports.name: getEffectiveMainGrip
exports.doc: Resolves the active Main Hand weapon grip ('1h' or '2h'). - Bows (`great_bow`) are designated 2-handed only. - If no Side Hand is equipped (`!slot2`), the Main Hand is automatically 2H.

exports.name: setMainWeaponGrip
exports.doc: Switches Main Hand weapon grip ('1h' <-> '2h') in the Equipment Screen. - Bows (`great_bow`) are designated 2-handed only and cannot switch to 1H. - If no Side Hand is equipped, Main Hand is automatically 2H. - Switching to 2H un-slots Side Hand (moving any distinct Side Hand item into Aux if Aux is empty) so Main Hand is 2H.

exports.name: unlockEquipmentItem
exports.doc: Unlocks a weapon, shield, quiver, or catalyst into `state.equipmentSlots.unlockedEquipment`. If already unlocked, increments `ownedWeaponCounts` up to 2 so Paired Stance can be used.

exports.name: unlockLevel2SecondaryWeapon
exports.doc: Unlocks the pilot's canonical Weapon Set 2 item (`startingWeapons[1]`) when reaching Level 2 (helping/resolving The Poe or salvaging Bedivere `[S]`).

exports.name: getWeaponActiveGemId
exports.doc: Resolves the active Gem modification (`Col 0..8`) for a given weapon/shield/quiver ID. - If explicitly modified in `state.equipmentSlots.weaponGemMods[weaponId]`, uses that Gem. - Otherwise, if an Action Mod is installed for the weapon's category, uses that Action Mod's primary Gem. - Otherwise returns `null` (Base column `0`).

exports.name: getWeaponGemCombatModifiers
exports.doc: Computes the stone-specific combat bonus for a weapon, shield, or quiver modified with a Gemstone (`Cols 0..8`).

exports.name: getWeaponGemVisuals
exports.doc: Resolves the sprite sheet column (`0..8`), Gem-colored blade trail / projectile VFX palette, and stone-specific combat bonus label for any weapon, shield, or quiver (`Rows 4–14`).

exports.name: modifyWeaponWithGem
exports.doc: Modifies a weapon, shield, or quiver with a Gem (`Col 0..8`) to shift its sprite column, tint its blade trails / projectiles with that Gem's color, and apply its stone-specific combat bonus. Gated behind Level 6 (`isStandardProgressionUnlocked`) or Sandbox Bypass.

exports.name: syncPostTutorialFrameLevel
exports.doc: Advances Frame Level from 6 up to 20 naturally as the pilot invests Gemstones into Pilot Skills, sockets Feat Nodes, generates Equipment/Weapon Mods, and clears bosses/trials.

exports.name: doesPilotMeetFeatEquipmentRequirement
exports.doc: Evaluates whether the pilot's currently equipped loadout satisfies a Feat's hardware requirement. In classless Project Orion, feats are gated ONLY by Pilot Skill Tier + Gemstones + Hardware/Weapon family, never by player class.

exports.name: fundPilotSkillWithGem
exports.doc: GEM USE 1 — PILOT SKILL LEVEL (Gems Permanently Consumed): Consumes 1 assigned Discipline Gem or Reactor Gem from inventory to raise a Combat Discipline Skill level (1–20). Unlocking skill levels opens the 5 Feat Tiers (I–V) and Feat Node availability.

exports.name: PlayerLightStatBreakdown
exports.doc: Structured stat breakdown for the pilot's derived Light stat (in tiles; base 5 = half one screen).

exports.name: computePlayerLightStatBreakdown
exports.doc: Computes the player's derived Light stat breakdown from base Light (`5.0` tiles) plus Feats, Hardware/Weapons/Items (e.g. Head Optics, Poe Lantern, Sensory Arrays), and active Skills/Spells. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: computeEffectivePlayerLightTiles
exports.doc: Computes the player's effective Light stat in tiles (base 5 = half one screen), modified by Feats, Hardware, Items, Skills, and Spells. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: adjustPlayerBaseLight
exports.doc: Applies a delta to the player's base Light stat (used by effects or sandbox tools). Mutates `state: OrionState` (`state.baseLight`).

exports.name: adjustEnemyBaseLight

exports.name: toggleFeatNodeGemSocket
exports.doc: GEM USE 2 — FEAT NODE SOCKETING (Gems Removed from Inventory, Retained in Build, Refunded on Unsocket): Installing the required Discipline + Reactor Gems unlocks and activates the Feat Node. exports.name: generateEquipmentModWithGems

exports.name: triggerEntityFlash
exports.doc: Triggers a fighting-game / Souls-style silhouette flash frame on an entity or player state.

exports.name: evaluatePositionalHitQuality
exports.doc: Evaluates positional accuracy ("sweet-spot" vs "sour-spot") for a melee strike or projectile impact. Critical hits are a spatial accuracy variable rather than a random chance variable: - Spear / Lance tip (`0.68 <= rNorm <= 1.05` & tight centerline): `1.35x` damage, `+40%` armor bypass. - Hammer / Mace / Axe head (`0.60 <= rNorm <= 0.98`): `1.35x` damage, `+40%` armor bypass. - Sword / Blade upper cutting sweet-spot (`0.54 <= rNorm <= 0.92` & centered arc): `1.30x` damage, `+35%` armor bypass. - Haft / hilt / sour-spot (`rNorm < 0.42`): `0.72x` glancing damage, `-35%` armor bypass (enemy armor is 35% more effective).

exports.name: isTargetInThrustCorridor
exports.doc: Linear piercing corridor test (for Short Spear, Avalon Lance, Stinger Thrust, Enraged Bors Lunge). Checks forward projection along `angle` within `[-4, length]` and perpendicular distance `<= halfWidth`.

exports.name: isTargetInDirectionalArc
exports.doc: Directional sector/arc test (for Long Sword slashes, Shotel cleaves, Hand Axe chops, Shield bashes).

exports.name: isTargetInImpactZone
exports.doc: Concentrated circular impact zone test centered at `forwardOffset` ahead of the attacker (for Mace slams & Ground tremors).

exports.name: applyDamageToLayers
exports.doc: Canonical 6 Damage Types (`Impact`, `Pierce`, `Blast`, `Beam`, `Pulse`, `Wave`) × 3 Defense Layers (`Shields`, `Armor` [`Ablative`, `Reactive`, `Hardened`, `Layered`], `Frame Integrity`).

exports.name: resolveEnemyMeleeAttacks
exports.doc: Resolves enemy melee/lunge/slam strikes against the player, including Perfect Block, Held Guard, and Inertia v0 impulse/displacement/stagger resolution.

exports.name: executeBasicAttackShot
exports.doc: Executes a single basic attack chain strike/shot (`activeSkillSlot === 0`) when `skillTellTimer` reaches 0.

exports.name: updateProjectiles
exports.doc: Updates active projectiles, wall collisions, and ranged Inertia v0 impacts (`J_ranged = projectile_weight × projectile_speed`).

exports.name: isTileBlockingSight
exports.doc: Checks whether a tile character blocks line-of-sight (solid wall '#', tree/pillar 'P', solid-phase desync barrier '%', or sealed gate 'G'/'M').

exports.name: hasTileLineOfSight
exports.doc: Ray-marches across the tile grid from `(x0, y0)` to `(x1, y1)` and returns `false` if any solid wall (`#`) or closed gate (`G`, `M`) blocks line-of-sight.

exports.name: canEnemyDetectPlayer
exports.doc: Evaluates whether an enemy `e` can currently detect and aggro onto the player: - Respects the spawn/reboot grace timer (`state.spawnGraceTimer > 0`), unless the player damaged `e`. - Uses the enemy's modifiable `Light` / vision radius (`(e.visionRadiusTiles ?? 5) * TILE_SIZE`, base 5 tiles = 80px) as its sight range (extended slightly if recently hurt or in boss/trial state). - Requires unobstructed tile line-of-sight (`hasTileLineOfSight`), preventing aggro through `#` walls or across sealed rooms.

exports.name: findNearestWaterTilePx
exports.doc: Finds the pixel center `(x, y)` of the nearest corrosive water tile (`'~'`) within `maxSearchRadiusTiles` of `(fromX, fromY)` in the active room grid. Used by Bog Wurms that must reach `'~'` before submerging.

exports.name: stepEnemyWithCollision
exports.doc: Moves an enemy along X and Y using axis-separated tile collision (`moveEntityX` / `moveEntityY`) so enemies cannot walk, kite, or lunge through solid `#` walls or closed gates.

exports.name: idlePatrolEnemy
exports.doc: Gently patrols an un-aggroed enemy in place while respecting wall and pillar collisions.

exports.name: INERTIA_CONSTANTS
exports.doc: Tunable classical-mechanics parameters (`inertia-v0.md §4`) governing impulse `J`, effective defender mass `m_eff`, and stability `S` deadband/recovery scaling.

exports.name: computeMomentumFraction
exports.doc: Computes forward momentum fraction `μ` (0 to 1) along a target/incoming directional axis. `μ = clamp(speed_toward_axis / reference_speed, 0, 1)` Returns `0` when stationary, moving away (`dot <= 0`), or moving perpendicular/sideways.

exports.name: computeEffectiveWeight
exports.doc: Computes Defender Effective Weight (`m_eff`) with directional charge bonus (§4, §6): `m_eff = m_defender × (1 + μ_defender)`

exports.name: computeStability
exports.doc: Computes Frame Stability (`S`, §5, OD-INR-06): Derived from frame weight + armor rating + hardware/feat/mod bonuses. Separate from weight `m` so a light frame can be built stable and a heavy frame is likely (not guaranteed) to be.

exports.name: computeMeleeImpulse
exports.doc: Computes Outgoing Melee Impulse (`J_melee`, §4): `attack_mass_eff = attack_weight + attacker_frame_weight × μ_attacker × commitment` `J_melee         = attack_mass_eff × attack_speed`

exports.name: computeRangedImpulse
exports.doc: Computes Outgoing Ranged Impulse (`J_ranged`, §2.6, §4, §9.6): `J_ranged = projectile_weight × projectile_speed` Explicitly includes NO shooter weight term.

exports.name: classifyInertiaOutcomeBand
exports.doc: Maps stability-reduced velocity change `Δv_eff` onto the 4 outcome bands (§4, §8, OD-INR-03): `'none' | 'flinch' | 'stagger' | 'knockback'`

exports.name: resolveHitInertia
exports.doc: Resolves a hit's physical displacement (`Δv`), reaction outcome band (`band(Δv_eff)`), recovery duration (`Δv_eff / (k2 · S)`), and hitstop freeze frames (§4, §5).

exports.name: resolveRecoil
exports.doc: Resolves Weapon Recoil using the exact same impulse rule (§7): `J_recoil      = projectile_weight × projectile_speed` `Δv_recoil     = J_recoil / m_shooter_frame` (no μ charge bonus) `Δv_recoil_eff = max(0, Δv_recoil - k1 · S)` `restriction   = Δv_recoil_eff / (k2 · S)`

exports.name: hasInertialTelemetryModEquipped
exports.doc: Checks whether the pilot currently has the Inertial Gyro-Telemetry equipment mod or sensory array installed. By design (§1, §8, user specification), HUD inertia telemetry is hidden unless this mod is equipped.

exports.name: resolvePlayerInertiaProfile
exports.doc: Computes the player mech's current Weight (`m`), Stability (`S`), Deadband (`k1 · S`), and Charge Capacity (`m_eff` max) from equipped chassis hardware, weapons, feats, and mods.

exports.name: resolveWeaponAttackInertiaSpec
exports.doc: Resolves numeric attack weight (`m_attack`), attack speed (`v_attack`), commitment (`c_atk`), and projectile weight (`m_projectile`) for any weapon action slot (0..4).

exports.name: resolveEnemyInertiaProfile
exports.doc: Resolves an enemy entity's Weight (`m`), Stability (`S`), and outgoing attack inertia parameters (§10). Ensures PvP/PvE Unification Law compliance: enemies use the exact same formulas as the player mech.

exports.name: formatInertiaOutcomeLabel
exports.doc: Formats an outcome band for visual/telemetry display.

exports.name: resolvePlayerSpriteParts
exports.doc: Resolves the pilot's active 3-piece mech visual loadout (Frame Plating [Torso/Legs], Shoulders/Arms, Head). Each slot resolves independently: supports the 12 baseline sets (0..11), additional sets (12+), and standalone individual pieces that do not belong to a full 3-piece set.

exports.name: computePlayerWeightRecoveryProfile
exports.doc: Computes the pilot's weight-scaled wind-down recovery sequence and physical stopping inertia from their equipped Frame Plating load class, active Weapon weight class, and overload state.

exports.name: stepPlayerGlideAnimation
exports.doc: Advances the player Mech's 4-frame Magic-Current Glide state machine (`state.glidePhase` & `state.glideFrame`).

exports.name: toCardinalFacing
exports.doc: Resolves an 8-way OrionDir into one of the 4 canonical sprite facings ('N' | 'S' | 'E' | 'W') so character chassis layers and weapon hardpoints are always 100% locked to the same 4 facings.

exports.name: isRenderableWeaponMount
exports.doc: Determines whether an equipped item ID should be visually rendered on the player sprite hardpoints. Excludes consumables (flasks, draughts, potions), gemstones, currency, and non-combat inventory items.

exports.name: drawPlayerWeaponMounts25D
exports.doc: Renders the pilot's three weapon hardpoints (`Main Hand [Right]`, `Side Hand [Left]`, and `Aux [Back]`) locked into the 4 canonical sprite facings ('N' | 'S' | 'E' | 'W') with locked-in relative coordinates. Excludes consumables (flasks, potions) and aligns depth sorting with the character chassis. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: drawCompositePlayerMech
exports.doc: Renders the modular player Mech sprite composed of 3 aligned `16x16` px armor layers (`plating`, `arms`, `head`) plus depth-sorted `Main Hand (Right)`, `Side Hand (Left)`, and `Aux (Back)` weapon mounts, with 1px post-processed outlines around each component. Locked to 4 canonical sprite facings ('N' | 'S' | 'E' | 'W') with locked-in weapon coordinates. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: createNewPilotGame
exports.doc: §2.4 Pilot Creation (LOCKED): Created at New Game: trait line selection, then pilot name, then start at Level 1 in the starting zone (M00 The Bog 0,0) with that trait line's default loadout.

exports.name: updatePlayerSystem
exports.doc: Step player movement, pit-fall recovery, [Y] Lock-On/Weapon Swap, [B] Tap/Hold Booster, [A] Jump/Interact, and Tutorial onboarding. Returns `false` if the frame should early-return (e.g., plummeting into a sinkhole or rebooting).

exports.name: isTileOpaqueToLight
exports.doc: Returns true if the tile at `(tx, ty)` is an opaque vision/light blocker (walls `#`, trees/pillars `P`, solid-phase desync walls `%`, or closed gates `G`/`M`).

exports.name: computeRayLightTransmission
exports.doc: Computes soft-edged dynamic line-of-sight transmission `[0..1]` from `(lx, ly)` to `(targetX, targetY)` by sampling a primary center ray and two slight perpendicular penumbra offsets.

exports.name: renderDepthSortedEntitiesAndProps
exports.doc: Renders depth-sorted room props, pickups, enemies, and the composite player Mech (including Main Hand [Right], Side Hand [Left], and Aux [Back] hardpoints). Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: getEastDirectionalTransform
exports.doc: Computes 2D canvas scale & rotation transforms for sprites authored with the character facing East ('E'). - East ('E'): identity (scaleX = 1, scaleY = 1, rot = 0) - West ('W'): horizontal flip (scaleX = -1, scaleY = 1, rot = 0) - South ('S'): +90 deg clockwise rotation (scaleX = 1, scaleY = 1, rot = +PI/2) - North ('N'): -90 deg counter-clockwise rotation (scaleX = 1, scaleY = 1, rot = -PI/2) - Intercardinals ('NE', 'SE', 'NW', 'SW'): East or West-mirrored with +/-45 deg rotation

exports.name: drawAetherFogWayfindingTells
exports.doc: Renders peripheral Æther mist veils and doorway path-density / Poe Lantern wayfinding tells. Supports both HUD modes. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: drawOutlinedCanvasText
exports.doc: Draws 1px outlined pixel text onto a 2D canvas context. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: drawCanonicalHud

exports.name: isNearSanctuaryRoom

exports.name: ensureExpanseGridAllocated

exports.name: regenerateWorldEnemiesAndOffPathTiles
exports.doc: Despawns all active/hibernated enemies, clears non-boss enemy cleared flags so standard enemies respawn, re-rolls the off-path Aether Fog seed, and resets dynamic off-path chunk tiles so they regenerate on death or fast travel.

exports.name: setExpanseGridTileAt

# Project Orion — World, Content & Base64 Asset Authoring Guide

Welcome to the **Project Orion** authoring manual. The cartridge is built around **recursive module auto-discovery** (`import.meta.glob`), a **five-tier nested spatial hierarchy** (`Biomes → Rooms → Maps → Areas → Regions`), a **globally classless, hardware-driven build architecture (`v0.8`)**, and a **unified classical-mechanics Inertia & Stability physics engine (`inertia-v0.md`)**.

> **The Golden Rule of Orion Authoring:**
> Unless new content requires a brand-new engine mechanic or a new route entry in `KEY_NODE_ROUTES`, **you never edit engine files or `index.ts` registries**. Dropping a new `.ts` file into the appropriate `database/` subfolder automatically registers it on boot.

---

## 0. Quick-Jump Code Anchor Map (`[ORION-ANCHOR: ID]`)

Every critical registry, world-composer boundary, and engine hook in the codebase is tagged with a standardized `// [ORION-ANCHOR: <ID>]` comment block. Search for any anchor ID below to jump directly to the exact block of code to inspect or edit:

| `[ORION-ANCHOR: U00-UNIVERSE-CATALOG]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/world/universe.ts` | The 20-World `u00` Universe catalog (`8 Major`, `7 Minor`, `5 Unstable`) and `specStatus: 'LOCKED' \| 'UNDEFINED'` world status flags. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-GLOB-REGISTRY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/world/index.ts` | Single polymorphic `import.meta.glob` scanner that auto-registers Regions, Areas, Maps, Rooms, Biomes, Tiles, Waystations, and Waygates. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: ASCII-CHAR-REGISTRY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/world/index.ts` | Centralized ASCII character resolver (`getTileDefinition`, `resolveRoomEnemyTypeAtChar`) and `getMasterAsciiCharacterRegistry()` collision audit. |

## 2. Authoring the 5-Tier World Hierarchy & Aether Fog Topology

### 2A. Aether Fog 5-Node Topology & Depth Progression (`[ORION-ANCHOR: AETHER-FOG-TOPOLOGY]`)
No outer room in Orion has a literal solid map border. Instead, `systems/world/worldTransitions.ts` routes cardinal doorways (`N`, `S`, `E`, `W`) through a dynamic 5-node Æther Fog graph with real-time HUD depth gauge and in-world environmental tells:
- **`key` Nodes**: Authored Points of Interest (Drop-Pod, Towns, Boss Sanctums, Waystations, Waygates) registered via `RoomDefinition` files and linked in `KEY_NODE_ROUTES` (`[ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-KEY-ROUTES]`).
- **`general` Nodes**: Dynamically generated corridor chunks that advance route progress (`1/N .. N/N`) between connected `key` nodes when `routeTotal > 0` in `KEY_NODE_ROUTES`.
- **`side` Nodes**: Off-path branches extending from `general` or `key` nodes; they do **not** advance route progress and lead either to an `end` node or a `loop` node.
- **`end` Nodes**: Terminal single-exit pockets featuring rolled rewards (`loot_cache`, `mini_boss`, `secret_switch`, or `dead_end`).
- **`loop` Nodes (Depth `1 .. clvl + 1`)**: Going deeper into the Æther fog scales up to `maxDepth = clvl + 1`. Defeating a boss at `maxDepth` clears the fog (`clearAetherFogOnBossDefeat`) and returns the player to their anchor node on the main path.

---

### 2B. Master ASCII Tile, Doodad & Enemy Spawn Character Registry (`[ORION-ANCHOR: ASCII-CHAR-REGISTRY]`)

1. **Terrain / Wall / Doodad Pass (`getTileDefinition(char, biomeId)`)**: Looks up `biome.tileTypes[char]` first, then falls back to global `TILE_REGISTRY[char]`, then defaults to `.` (`floor`) so enemy spawn characters automatically sit on walkable floor tiles.
2. **Enemy / NPC Spawn Pass (`resolveRoomEnemyTypeAtChar(char, biomeId)` at `[ORION-ANCHOR: ENTITY-SPAWN-ROOM]`)**: Looks up `biome.enemySpawnTypes?.[char]` first, then falls back to global `CHAR_TO_ENEMY_TYPE[char]`.

---

## 3. Inertia & Stability Physics System (`docs/INERTIA_SYSTEM.md`)

Project Orion uses a **weight-vs-weight classical mechanics Inertia & Stability model** (`src/cartridges/orion/systems/inertiaSystem.ts`) instead of a static poise pool:
- **Weight (`m`) & Directional Charge (`μ`)**: Controls physical displacement (`Δv = J / m_eff`, where `m_eff = m_defender × (1 + μ_defender)` and `μ` only applies when moving into the incoming hit).
- **Stability (`S`)**: Derived from frame weight + armor + leg stabilizers + feats; controls the shrug-off deadband (`k1·S`) and hit recovery speed (`Δv_eff / (k2·S)`).
- **Melee vs. Ranged Impulse (`J`)**: Melee impulse combines attack weight + attacker body weight × `μ_attacker` × commitment factor; Ranged impulse is strictly `projectile_weight × projectile_speed` (independent of shooter weight).
- **Ranged Recoil (`§7`)**: Uses the exact same impulse equation (`Δv_recoil = J_recoil / m_shooter_frame`) with deadband `k1·S`, so heavier and more stable frames suffer less movement restriction while firing heavy weapons.
- **No HUD Clutter by Default**: Inertia and Stability numbers are never shown on the default HUD; full physics telemetry is available in the `MECH STATUS` Satchel tab, and live HUD readouts only appear when the **Inertial Gyro-Telemetry Array** equipment mod is installed in Sensory B.

# PROJECT ORION — CODE RULES
### Rules for any AI or human writing Orion code (Gemini / AI Studio system instruction)
*Version: 0.1 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Status: Active*

---

## STATUS KEY

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| LOCKED | Stated by the project owner as required. Do not weaken without an explicit design session. |
| PROPOSED | Drafted wording or specifics. Pending owner confirmation. |
| DERIVED | Observed in the repo at the baseline commit (section 9). Match it. |
| UNDEFINED | Known gap. Ask before assuming. |

---

## 1. COMMENTING

- **License header.** Every `.ts` / `.tsx` file starts with exactly:
  ```ts
  /**
   * @license
   * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
   */
  ```
- **JSDoc on every exported function, type, interface and registry.** The first sentence says what it does and when it applies. Put identifiers, coordinates and concrete values in backticks (`"rx,ry"`, `10 x 9`, `cx=3..4`).
- **Comment the why and the invariants,** not what the line already says. Put units in names or comments (`px`, `tiles`, `ms`, `frames`).
- **Anchors.** Registries, world-composer boundaries and engine hooks carry a `// [ORION-ANCHOR: UPPER-KEBAB-ID]` comment. Never duplicate or delete an ID. A new anchor must be added to the anchor table in `docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md` in the same change.
- **Forbidden:** commented-out code, `TODO` / `FIXME` (record gaps as an Open Decision with an `OD-` id in the relevant doc), `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `any`.
- **Spec-driven code** cites its source section in the JSDoc (for example `mechanics-v1.md §9`).

---

## 2. MODULARITY

- **Content is data, one entity per file.** Enemies, weapons, items, equipment, rooms, maps and tiles live as separate files under `database/<domain>/` and are picked up by `import.meta.glob`. New content means a new file. Do not edit engine files or registry `index.ts` files to add content.
- **Engine code goes in its domain folder:** `types/`, `systems/combat/`, `systems/render/`, `systems/world/`, `ui/hud/`, `ui/satchel/`. A new system goes in the matching folder. Do not grow an existing large file.
- **Import direction:** `database/` imports only from `types/` and sibling data. `systems/` never imports from `ui/`.
- **Pure functions** for math and resolution. Anything that mutates game state takes `state: OrionState` explicitly and says so in its JSDoc.
- **No magic numbers.** Shared dimensions and tuning values live in `constants.ts` (`SCREEN_W`, `SCREEN_H`, room `COLS` / `ROWS`, and so on). Read it before using a number.
- **File size.** Plan a split before a file passes 1,000 lines.
- **Both HUD modes.** Any HUD feature states in its JSDoc whether it supports the React overlay HUD, the pixel canvas HUD, or both.

---

## 3. MEMORY SAFETY

- **Every listener, timer, frame request and subscription has a cleanup in the same module.** React code uses a `useEffect` cleanup return. Every `setTimeout` / `setInterval` / `requestAnimationFrame` has a matching `clear*` / `cancel*`.
- **No unbounded growth.** Any module-level `Map`, `Set`, array or cache has a size cap or a defined clearing event (room change, waystation rest, and so on). State the eviction rule in its JSDoc.
- **Reuse heavy objects.** Offscreen canvases, bitmaps and audio nodes are created once, reused, and released (set to `null`, or `width = 0` for canvases) when replaced.
- **No allocation in per-frame paths.** No new arrays, objects or closures inside update or draw loops. Reuse buffers.
- **Remove entities everywhere.** When an entity is removed from a list, remove it from every index, map and target reference that points to it.
- **Types.** No `any`. No non-null assertion (`!`) without a comment explaining why it is safe.

---

## 4. NETWORK SAFETY

- **The Orion cartridge makes no network calls today.** Do not add one unless the request explicitly asks for it.
- **If a network call is approved:**
  - Keep all network code in a single module.
  - HTTPS only, with a hard-coded host allowlist.
  - Use an `AbortController` timeout and a response size cap.
  - Treat every response as untrusted: validate its shape before use.
  - Never pass network data to `eval`, `Function` or `innerHTML`.
  - No tokens, keys or secrets in client code or in the repo.
  - The game must still work fully offline.
- **Persisted data (`localStorage`):**
  - Wrap every read and parse in `try` / `catch` and validate the result.
  - New save fields are optional, with defaults applied on load, so older saves still open.
  - Use the existing key constants. Never store credentials.

---

## 5. HOUSEKEEPING

- **Docs change in the same commit as the code.** A new anchor updates `docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md`. New equipment or feats update `docs/EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md`. A new gap becomes an Open Decision with an `OD-` id.
- **Imports:** relative paths, alphabetized inside the braces, no unused imports or variables.
- **Formatting:** single quotes, two-space indent, trailing commas.
- **Naming:** `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` constants, `camelCase` functions, `PascalCase` types. File names follow the neighbors in the same folder.
- **Before handing back:** `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) passes and `npm run build` succeeds.
- **No leftovers:** no debug logging, no dead code, no stray files.

---

## 6. RESPONSE PROTOCOL

1. Restate the request in one line.
2. List the files you read.
3. Make the change, as complete files or exact diffs.
4. List files touched, new exports, and anything `UNVERIFIED`.
5. If a rule here conflicts with the request, say which rule and ask.

---

## 7. FILE STRUCTURE AND CONDENSING

- The current file layout is **not permanent**. As the codebase grows, files may be merged or condensed.
- Condensing must keep **wiki-like editability**: a reader can find the one place that owns a topic, edit it, and not touch anything else.
- Condensing **never removes a current function or export.**
- Anchors survive any move. Update the docs that name a moved file in the same commit.

---

## 8. DESIGN GUARDRAILS

*DERIVED — from the project docs. See `docs/` for the sources.*

- PvP and PvE share identical rules. No mode-specific balance tracks.
- Player stats are static. Progression unlocks slots and systems, never numbers.
- Damage, healing and feat values are expressed against the Base Combat Unit (`1× BCU = 54`).
- Every skill has a windup tell.

---

## 9. VERIFIED BASELINE (Updated 2026-10-30)

*DERIVED — re-check after major refactors.*

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `.ts` / `.tsx` files under `src/cartridges/orion` | 155 |
| License header on every file | Yes (155 of 155) |
| Files with no JSDoc at all | 0 |
| `// [ORION-ANCHOR: …]` anchors in code | 23 |
| `any`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `TODO`, `FIXME` | 0 |
| Network calls (`fetch`, XHR, WebSocket, `http(s)://` in code) | 0 |
| `addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` | 0 / 0 |
| `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` | Paired via tracked timer refs & unmount cleanup (`ui/OrionGameMenu.tsx`) |
| `requestAnimationFrame` / `cancelAnimationFrame` | 2 / 2 (`ui/OrionHud.tsx`, `ui/satchel/SatchelCanvases.tsx`) |
| Files over 1,000 lines | 9 (largest: `systems/combat/skillExecution.ts`, 2,860) |
| Docs anchors missing from code | None (`0`) |
| Code anchors missing from docs | None (`0`) |

---

*CODE_RULES.md | Project Orion internal documentation*
*Version 0.1 — Initial rules for AI-assisted coding. Requirements from the owner; wording and specifics derived from the repo.*

# Project Orion — Index

*A field guide to the Shattered Worlds, the road through Belldor, and the canonical documentation index*

---

## Documentation Directory (`src/cartridges/orion/docs/`)

| Document | Scope & Contents |
| --- | --- |
| **`docs/INDEX.md`** *(this file)* | Narrative worldbuilding, the Shattered Worlds, Belldor campaign stages (`M00 The Bog`, `Camelot Border Town`), starting loadout kits, and documentation map. |
| **`docs/CODE_RULES.md`** | Mandatory engineering rules for any human or AI authoring Orion code: Apache-2.0 license headers, JSDoc contracts, `[ORION-ANCHOR]` discipline, modularity, memory/network safety, and baseline verification. |
| **`docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md`** | Technical architecture, modular domain systems (`types/`, `systems/combat/`, `systems/render/`, `systems/world/`, `ui/hud/`, `ui/satchel/`), `[ORION-ANCHOR]` jump table, 5-tier world hierarchy, and Base64 asset recipes. |
| **`docs/EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md`** | Full `v0.8` canonical catalog of 29 magitech weapons, 6 coreplates, 6 reactors, 18 aux/utility systems, 18 optics/sensors, 12 limb actuators, and 97 classless feats. |
| **`docs/INERTIA_SYSTEM.md`** | Working specification (`inertia-v0.md`) for the simplified classical mechanics Inertia & Stability model (`Δv = J / m_eff`, Stability `S`, directional charge `μ`, rock-paper-scissors triangle, and recoil). |

---

## The Short Version

The worlds were once linked by waygates. Then something was taken that should have stayed, and the links began to drift. You are a pilot: a being no world claims, immune to the æther between worlds, and able to bond with the war machines called mechs. Every faction wants you. None of them trust you.

This guide walks the road as it is currently planned, from your first step in the bog to the edge of what has been built. Past that point, the guide says **more to come**.

---

## Part I — The World

### The Waygates

At the heart of every known world stands a waygate, a colossal archway of stone, root and mineral that looks more like a canyon mouth than a building. There are no controls and no inscriptions. You walk through, and the gate reads your ætheric signature and carries you on. No one knows how it picks a destination. No one knows who built them. Scholars believe they were anchors that kept the worlds in alignment, and that belief fits what happened next.

### The Æther

Between the worlds lies the æther, an active and hostile medium. Living tissue that touches it disintegrates at once. The proof is infamous: on an interworld vessel, a single strand of an elven bride's hair crossed a flux-field breach, and she died instantly. Her death was taken for murder, and two elven clans fought an eight-year war before the truth came out.

Vessels can cross the æther only by holding a protective flux field around the hull. The æther can be resisted. It has never been tamed.

### The Mining Operation

A dwarven civilization once mined a rare crystal. Nothing happened at first. Then landscapes shifted without cause, ruins appeared where none had stood, and the stars stopped matching the records. The crystals were **tuning crystals**, calibration structures that kept the worlds synchronized.

> Worlds did not break. They drifted.

This drift is called **desynchronization**, and it is still happening.

### The Pilots

Pilots appeared only after the catastrophe. No world claims them, and no record of them exists before it. They can walk through the æther unprotected and bond with mechs at once. People say they are remnants of the catastrophe, or echoes, or walking fractures in reality. Nobody has proven anything. Factions recruit them anyway.

### The Fragmented Present

Distances between worlds now fluctuate. Some worlds drift closer, and others recede out of reach. The powers that thrive are the ones holding waygates, interworld vessels and strategic resources. The ones that struggle are cut off from their trade routes or stranded on drifting worlds. Some worlds have simply gone silent. War is constant.

---

## Part II — The Worlds

| World | Culture |
| --- | --- |
| **Belldor (Camelot)** | Arthurian knights and grail mythology |
| Tyrranus | Greek and Roman |
| Orion | Dwarven |
| Novarin | Orc |
| Chyme | Draconic |
| Golem | Desert |
| New Novarin | Elven |
| Sin | Underworld |

Seven **minor worlds** (Sylvis, Vox, Victor, Jager, Ferrous, Ebony, Ivory) and five **unstable worlds** (Aurora, Rhyme, Siren, Lennus, Malleus) also exist. The unstable worlds are in severe desynchronization, and reaching them may be intermittent or dangerous.

Your road begins on Belldor.

---

## Part III — Belldor

> **Belldor teaches you how to fight. Every other world tests whether you learned.**

Before the catastrophe, Camelot was a center of magic and governance with one of the largest waygates in the network. Now regions of it phase in and out of alignment, cities flicker between ruin and restoration, and its ruling authority is gone. Several factions fight over the waygate, and all of them recruit pilots.

The campaign on Belldor is built as a lesson. You are never handed a tool before the world gives you a reason to need it, and the numbers on your mech do not grow. Two pilots at the same stage are equally strong, and what separates them is what they choose to do.

### Choosing Your Starting Loadout Kit (`v0.8` Classless Spec)

Your mech is a modular war machine, and **Project Orion has no player-facing classes**. Six pre-configured **Starting Loadout Kits** are available at Pilot Creation so you begin with a coherent frame, reactor, and weapon pairing—none of them locks you in. Any pilot can equip any weapon, coreplate, utility system, or feat as long as they meet the hardware and gemstone requirements. See `docs/EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md` for the full catalog of 29 magitech weapons, 6 coreplates, 6 reactors, 18 aux/utility systems, 18 optics/sensors, 12 limb actuators, and 97 feats.

| Starting Kit | Frame Model | Reactor | Base Load | Lv.6 Tactical Utility (`Action 6`) | Starting Role & Design Direction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Bastion Striker** | `PNSY W416` | Ichor | Medium | PNSY D-0g Repair Drone | Frontline striker. Aggressive, high-throughput, runs hot. |
| **Fortress Siege** | `RAD HAU` | Ichor | Super-Heavy | RAD R463 Fathomless System | Super-heavy artillery. Burst damage, natural presence, slow. |
| **Dawnforge Vanguard** | `Trinity DE-14` | Mana | Heavy | TI Lightwell Recovery System | Defensive anchor. Draws focus, protects allies, sustains shields. |
| **Phantom Recon** | `VX Phantom` | Ether | Light | VX Smoke Dispersal System | Stealth striker. Ambush and burst, lightest frame. |
| **Arclight Artillery** | `ARC Arclight` | Ether | Light | ARC Rift Anchor | Energy artillery. Sustained beams, long range. |
| **Sanctum Support** | `SANC Sanctum` | Mana | Medium | SANC Radiant Ward Projector | Support anchor. Reinforces shields/armor, vents heat, and manages target priority. |

#### The Three Layers of a Build (`Pilot → Frame → Equipment`)
- **Pilot (`Skills`)**: Created at New Game (`Starting Kit → Pilot Callsign → Level 1 in M00 The Bog`) and listed on the Load Game roster. Six **Combat Disciplines** progress through gemstone investment (locked out during the `Levels 1–5` tutorial until `Level 6: Border Town Complete`) and unlock **Feat Tiers (`I–V`)**.
- **Frame (`Feats`)**: **97 Canonical Feats** across Tiers I–V. **System Feats** step up Load Capacity (`light → medium → heavy → superheavy`); **Interface Feats** tune combat behavior and weapon/hardware synergies within a fixed static budget. Feats are gated by Skill Tier, Gemstone sockets, and equipped Hardware/Weapon families—never by class—and can be unsocketed and refunded at any time.
- **Equipment (`13 Slots + Mods`)**: Weapon Set 1 (`Weapon 1–2`), Weapon Set 2 (`Weapon 3–4`), Tactical Utility (`1`, `Action 6`), Aux (`Aux 1–4`, `Actions 7–10`), Belt (`4`, `Actions 7–10`), plus `Coreplate`, `Reactor Core`, `Optics`, `Sensory A/B`, `Arms`, and `Legs`. Action Modifications alter behavior with a paired drawback.
- **Inertia & Stability (`docs/INERTIA_SYSTEM.md`)**: Hit reactions (`none`, `flinch`, `stagger`, `knockback`), hitstop freeze frames, and ranged recoil restriction are governed by the unified impulse-momentum model (`Δv = J / m_eff`) and frame Stability (`S`).

### The Æther Fog

Belldor does not hold still. Beyond the places that were built, the land frays into **æther fog**: stretches of the same ruined country that shift, fold back on themselves and refuse to stay mapped. It is what desynchronization feels like from the ground. Nothing in it is fixed, and a pilot who has been through it once cannot be sure the same road will be there twice. The fog is also what makes the world larger than it looks. There is no wall at the edge of the map, only more fog.

**Density.** The fog gets thicker the farther in you go, and everything gets worse with it. Enemies grow more aggressive, the mist hangs heavier, and the ground becomes harder to cross. Pilots are immune to the æther itself, so the æther is not what hurts you. The danger is the environment it creates, and nothing in it is safe.

**The path.** The fog is built around authored places: towns, boss sanctums, waystations and waygates. Between them lie corridors that carry you from one place to the next, with branches off to side pockets that hold a reward, a fight or a hidden switch. The game nudges you along the path, but you never have to follow it. You can wander the fog all day if you want to.

**Going deeper.** Some branches lead into the fog proper, and each room is one step deeper than the last. Until you reach the deepest room, you can always turn around and retrace your steps, and every room back toward the path is as safe as it was when you passed through. The deepest room is different. It holds a boss that must be cleared, and clearing it returns you to the last place you stood on the main path. The depth where the boss waits is not the same everywhere. A shallow pocket may bottom out after two or three rooms, and a deep one after five or more.

**The Lantern.** The Poe's gift is the one tool that reads the fog. It shows where the fog deepens and what is waiting beneath the water, and it never points you toward the story.

---

## Part IV — The Road Through Belldor

### Stage 1: The Bog (Levels 1–2)

You arrive in a drowned maze of fallen trees and the ruins of an old temple or monastery. The air is thick with æther. The water is not the æther's doing, but it is dangerous in its own right: **bog water is corrosive**. It eats armor, and it does not care who is standing in it. That includes the things hunting you. The marsh lies inside Belldor's æther fog, so the two overlap here, but they are separate things. The bog is not æther, and not every stretch of fog holds bog water.

**What lives here**

- **Orc pairs.** Orcs always come as a Warrior and a Scout. The Warrior is a shield-bearing brawler who closes distance and hits hard. The Scout stays back, shoots from range, and tries to slip away to heal if you hurt it. Kill the Scout first, but don't let the Warrior reach you.
- **The Bog Wurm.** A snake-like hybrid of machine and flesh, with glowing ætheric veins running through its mechanical parts. It hides invisible beneath the water, strikes first, and retreats to heal when hurt. The bog is its friend, and it knows it.

**The Poe.** Somewhere in the maze you will find a small floating lantern-spirit that calls itself "Poe." Every Poe says the same thing about itself, and they only manifest where the æther is thick. Helping it back to its lantern will earn you a gift. It reveals what hides beneath the water and where the fog grows deeper, and it will change how you fight the Wurm. Ignoring it or killing it is also allowed. The way out of the bog stays hidden until you deal with it one way or another.

**Bedivere.** Further on lies the body of a knight who was heading for the border town and never made it. He carries a **signet ring** and a **numbered list** of items that makes no sense yet. Taking the ring has consequences in the next zone. Leaving it has consequences too. The game will not explain the weight of that choice.

### Stage 2: Camelot Border Town (Levels 3–6)

The road out of the bog drops you at the outer edge of a large contested settlement, the gateway between orc territory and Camelot's interior. No one governs it, and no part of it is safe.

**The sickness.** Everyone here suffers from **grail sickness**. Some people are calm enough to trade. Some will turn on you if you linger. Some are feral and attack on sight. Which is which is not always obvious.

**The ring.** Knights' loyalists in town see anyone carrying Bedivere's ring as a grave robber. If you took it, loyalist merchants will not deal with you, and some will attack outright. Non-loyalists don't care either way. The ring is also your key to the dungeon subplot.

**The districts**

| District | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Outer Perimeter** | Collapsed walls, abandoned orc siege gear, burnt waystations. Where you arrive and the first line against invasion. |
| **Market District** | A half-working market where buildings flicker between intact and ruined every few seconds and the day-night cycle races. Container caches hold parts, consumables and blueprints. |
| **Barracks Quarter** | The former knight garrison, now a factional holdout. Strong fortifications, better loot, and the patrol routes of the three knights. |
| **Cathedral District** | Burnt grail tapestries, a defiled altar, bells that ring out of rhythm. The place to learn what the catastrophe did to Camelot. |

**Orc raids.** The orcs of the nearby encampment raid the town without warning. A war horn sounds, the screen pulses red, and the exit back to the bog is sealed until the raid is dealt with. During a raid **every NPC goes feral**. The orcs go after NPCs before they go after you, so you can fight for the town, stay out of it, or run for the dungeon and leave the market to be looted. If you save enough people, the survivors will remember it.

**The Three Knights**

| Knight | Fights as | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Percival**, Grail Knight | A guardian. A shield wall that has to be flanked or broken, and a charge that closes distance. | Protects his comrades. Recovers shields when badly hurt, so don't let up. |
| **Tristan**, Corrupted Ranger | A kiting archer. Volleys of arrows, smoke to escape corners, and a sight that finds you behind cover. | Fragile if you catch him. Punishes anyone who sits still. |
| **Bors**, Berserk Striker | A relentless brawler who grows stronger with every hit he lands. | Turns enraged at half health. His killing lunge is telegraphed, and deadly if you miss it. |

You can take them one at a time, or all at once for a better reward, a feat called **Knight's Oath**, which gives permanent bonus damage against Camelot's enemies.

**The Dungeon Door.** At the edge of the cathedral a stone staircase descends into mist, past carved grail symbols and flickering statues. This is the last gate before the Camelot waygate, and there are three planned ways to open it:

- **By force.** Defeat all three knights and take a Grail Fragment from each.
- **By exploration.** Find three hidden switches: one behind a desynchronizing wall in the market, one under the cathedral altar, and one in a secret armory room in the barracks.
- **By trust.** Earn the goodwill of the town through enough successful raid defenses. Carrying the ring makes this far harder.

Which of these will be live in the final game is still being decided.

### Stage 3: What Waits Below

Below the staircase lie lore, the key to the Camelot waygate, and the end of your first road. **Planned, but not yet designed.**

---

## Part V — Secrets

Some of what Belldor holds is not on the main road.

- **Bedivere's list.** Its items read as nonsense. They are scattered across more than one zone. Whoever collects them all and returns to the bog will find the water has been waiting. Something half machine and half serpent, an old name twisted by the æther, answers to the **Lady of the Lake**.
- **Hidden caches** in the border town hold blueprints, and every piece of gear in this game has to be found, crafted or earned.

---

## Part VI — After Belldor

By the time you are done here, you will have everything the game has to teach. Your frame, your weapons and your skills are all yours. From then on, progress is about **how** you fight and not how strong you are. A new weapon moves differently and does not hit harder, and different worlds ask different things of the same pilot.

**More to come:**

- **The Orc Encampment** where the raids begin.
- **The deep dungeon** beneath the border town, and the **Camelot waygate**.
- **Camelot's interior** beyond the gate.
- **The other worlds**: Tyrranus, Orion, Novarin, Chyme, Golem, New Novarin and Sin, plus the minor and unstable worlds.
- **Æther incursions.** Pilots can project their mechs across the æther into other pilots' worlds, as defenders or as attackers. The first incursion is an opt-in event somewhere after Belldor, and you can switch back out at any time with no penalty.
- **Queued 3v3 and 5v5 modes**, unlocked by exploration rather than level.
- **The truth about the pilots**, the waygates and the tuning crystals.

> The truth is not lost. It is unfolding.

---

# PROJECT ORION — INERTIA SYSTEM
### Weight, Momentum, Stability, and Hit Reaction — Simplified Physics Model
*Version: 0.1 | Updated: 2026-10-28 | Status: Active*

---

## HOW TO USE THIS DOCUMENT

This document is self-contained. It does not require any other Project Orion file. Section 1 gives the minimum game context needed. Everything else is the inertia system itself.

Scope is **inertia only**: how hits, recoil, and movement state combine to push, stagger, or ignore a mech. Glide handling, the stationary "Anchored" state, stealth, buffs/feats/mods, and hyper armor are explicitly out of scope (see §10).

Every claim carries a source tag. Do not treat PROPOSED material as decided.

---

## STATUS KEY

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| LOCKED | Finalized. Do not revise without explicit design session. |
| PROPOSED | Under discussion. Pending confirmation. |
| DERIVED | Not explicitly decided — inferred from other locked documentation. |
| UNDEFINED | Known gap. Not yet resolved. Blocks dependent systems. |

## SOURCE TAGS

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [A] | Stated by the design author in this working session |
| [P1] | Stated in Project Orion documentation (Tier 1 for this project) |
| [PHYS] | Standard classical mechanics, unsourced here (Tier 4 under the author's rubric; every equation is unit-checkable) |
| [INF] | Inferred by the drafting assistant; needs author confirmation |

---

## TABLE OF CONTENTS

1. [Context](#1-context)
2. [Author Design Intent](#2-author-design-intent)
3. [Physics Basis](#3-physics-basis)
4. [Model](#4-model)
5. [Stability](#5-stability)
6. [Charge Modifier and Rock-Paper-Scissors](#6-charge-modifier-and-rock-paper-scissors)
7. [Recoil](#7-recoil)
8. [Player Legibility Requirements](#8-player-legibility-requirements)
9. [Validation Properties](#9-validation-properties)
10. [Parked Items and Known Interactions](#10-parked-items-and-known-interactions)
11. [Open Decisions](#11-open-decisions)
12. [Glossary Candidates](#12-glossary-candidates)

---

## 1. CONTEXT

*DERIVED*

- Project Orion is a mobile isometric magitech mech action game with persistent, MOBA-inspired action combat. [P1]
- PvP and PvE share identical rules. No separate PvP modifiers. (The Unification Law.) [P1]
- Movement is a glide system using latent magic currents. The player does not walk. [A]
- Frames have weight classes: light, medium, heavy, superheavy. Weapons have weight classes: light, medium, heavy. No numeric weights exist yet. [P1]
- A Stability stat already exists, defined as "recoil absorption, stagger resistance, recovery from impacts," and described as derived from armor + weight. [P1]
- Damage is a separate system: Base Combat Unit (BCU) = 54 damage per reference weapon chain; frame integrity is 200; armor uses a threshold / rating / durability model. [P1]
- **Inertia must not change damage numbers.** It governs displacement, interruption, and recovery only. This keeps all BCU validation intact. [INF]
- Relevant design laws: every ability has a visible tell (Law 1); CC durations are fixed and identical in PvE and PvP (Law 2); stats are marginal and action is primary (Law 6, PROPOSED). [P1]
- Meta stats are not displayed to the player; only visible state is. [P1]

---

## 2. AUTHOR DESIGN INTENT

*PROPOSED — author-stated*

1. Movement weight and recovery frames are the first systems that give the game a "mech" feel. [A]
2. Heavier frames reach close to the same top speed as lighter ones, but handle worse. [A]
3. Heavier frames suffer less movement restriction while attacking, most noticeably with heavier weapons. This also accounts for recoil. [A]
4. Poise is not wanted as a stat. Pseudo-poise is "weight vs weight." [A]
5. Each attack has a speed and a weight, giving it an inertia. The character also has inertia. [A]
6. Ranged attacks do **not** include shooter weight in outgoing force. If recoil exists, shooter weight is not applicable to the shot. [A]
7. Recoil restriction depends on frame weight: a heavier frame absorbs more. [A]
8. A frame stability value is required. Heavier frames are likely more stable, but this is not guaranteed. A superheavy simply takes a hit better. Spells, skills, and hyper armor may modify this later. [A]
9. A charging heavy gains a resistance modifier. [A]
10. The system should work as "dynamic rock paper scissors." [A]
11. It must be simple enough for a player to understand without learning physics. [A]
12. All values must be modifiable by buffs, feats, mods, and similar sources, because the Marauder lore allows a stationary "doom machine" build. (Hooks only; see §10.) [A]
13. Historic feat tiers do not need to be considered. [A]

## 3. PHYSICS BASIS

*DERIVED*

[PHYS] Simplified classical mechanics:

```
momentum        p = m · v
impulse         J = Δp
velocity change Δv = J / m
recoil          Δv_shooter = −(m_projectile · v_projectile) / m_shooter
                (conservation of momentum)
```

Key observation [INF]: one rule, `Δv = J / m`, covers hits, recoil, and knockback.

**Intentional departure from physics [A]:** in real mechanics a defender's own velocity affects only relative velocity and gives no resistance bonus. This system deliberately gives a defender who is charging into a hit a resistance bonus (§6).

Terminology: "weight" in this document means mass.

## 4. MODEL

*PROPOSED*

### Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `m` | Weight of a body or object (frame, attack, projectile) |
| `v` | Speed along the relevant axis |
| `μ` | Forward momentum fraction, 0 to 1. `μ = clamp(speed_toward_incoming_hit / reference_speed, 0, 1)`. Zero when moving away or sideways. |
| `S` | Frame stability (§5) |
| `k1`, `k2` | Tuning constants. UNDEFINED. |

`reference_speed` is UNDEFINED (OD-INR-01).

### Equations

```
Defender effective weight
  m_eff = m_defender × (1 + μ_defender)

Melee impulse
  attack_mass_eff = attack_weight + attacker_frame_weight × μ_attacker
  J_melee         = attack_mass_eff × attack_speed

Ranged impulse
  J_ranged = projectile_weight × projectile_speed
  (no shooter term)

Hit reaction
  Δv       = J / m_eff
  Δv_eff   = max(0, Δv − k1·S)
  recovery = Δv_eff / (k2·S)
  outcome  = band(Δv_eff)   →  none | flinch | stagger | knockback
```

### Notes

- Both sides of a melee hit use the same shape: a base weight plus a momentum-scaled bonus. [INF]
- A restitution (bounce) factor was considered and folded into tuning for simplicity. Whether it should vary per attack is OD-INR-08. [INF]
- Band thresholds are UNDEFINED (OD-INR-03).
- Whether `recovery` is continuous (as above) or snapped to fixed values is UNDEFINED (OD-INR-09). See §10 for the conflict with fixed CC durations.

## 5. STABILITY

*PROPOSED*

`S` is a separate, modifiable value. It is **not** simply frame weight, so that a light frame can be built stable and a heavy frame is only *likely* to be.

| Axis | Controlled by | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Displacement | Weight (`m`) | How hard the body is pushed |
| Reaction | Stability (`S`) | Whether the body reacts at all, and how fast it recovers |

Consequences [INF]:

- A superheavy gets both benefits by default.
- A light frame with high `S` is pushed far but recovers fast.
- A single `S` drives both jobs (deadband and recovery) via two constants. Splitting into two values is deferred unless playtesting requires it. [A, decision accepted]

Default derivation: from frame weight plus components (armor, stabilizers). Exact function UNDEFINED (OD-INR-06). [P1 says "derived from armor + weight"]

## 6. CHARGE MODIFIER AND ROCK-PAPER-SCISSORS

*PROPOSED — triangle confirmed by author*

The charge bonus is **directional**: it applies only while moving into the incoming hit. A frame fleeing or sidestepping has `μ = 0`. [A, INF]

| Beats | Because | Loses to |
|---|---|---|
| Charging heavy | Small hits fall under the stability deadband and the charge bonus raises `m_eff` | A big slow hit |
| Big slow hit | Enough `J` to overcome the charge bonus | Evasion or sidestep (the hit has a readable tell) |
| Evasion or sidestep | Charge direction is fixed; off-axis, `μ` drops to 0 | Charging heavy |

Triangle: [A]. Mapping onto the equations: [INF].

Caveat [INF]: if `J` were based on relative velocity, a charging defender would take a larger hit and also resist more. To avoid this, `J` uses the attacker's own speed only, and the defender's `μ` carries the entire charge effect.

## 7. RECOIL

*PROPOSED*

```
J_recoil          = projectile_weight × projectile_speed
Δv_recoil         = J_recoil / m_shooter_frame
Δv_recoil_eff     = max(0, Δv_recoil − k1·S)
movement_restriction ∝ Δv_recoil_eff / (k2·S)
```

- Uses base frame weight; the charge bonus `μ` is not applied, because there is no incoming hit. [INF]
- Heavier, more stable frames ignore light recoil and recover faster from heavy recoil, producing the author's "less movement restriction while attacking" with no special-case rule. [A, INF]

## 8. PLAYER LEGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

*PROPOSED*

The player should be able to learn three rules from play, with no numbers shown:

1. Charging makes you hard to push.
2. Big slow hits break a charge.
3. Sidestepping beats a charge.

This requires [INF]:

- Distinct visible outcomes for shrugged-off, flinch, stagger, and knockback.
- A visible charge state, so a mid-charge heavy can be recognized.
- Few outcome bands (three outcomes plus "none").

---

## 9. VALIDATION PROPERTIES

*PROPOSED*

Any implementation or tuning pass must satisfy:

1. Heavier defender → smaller `Δv`, all else equal.
2. Higher `S` → smaller `Δv_eff` and shorter recovery.
3. Defender moving toward the hit → larger `m_eff`.
4. Defender moving away or sideways → no charge bonus.
5. Larger `attack_weight × attack_speed` → larger `J`; values must exist where a big slow hit overcomes a charging heavy.
6. Ranged `J` is independent of shooter weight.
7. Recoil effect decreases as frame weight and `S` increase.
8. Inertia never alters damage dealt or taken.
9. Identical behavior in PvP and PvE.
